questions.question_text: Which of the following is a consistently observed neuroradiological finding in elderly people with late-onset depression?

options.text: Decreased hippocampal volume
Decreased volume of basal ganglia
Frontotemporal cortex atrophy
Decreased volume of amygdala
Enlarged lateral ventricles

correct_answer.text: Enlarged lateral ventricles

correct_answers.text: Enlarged lateral ventricles

questions.explanation: Decreased hippocampal volume and decreased volume of basal ganglia are observed in patients with unipolar depressive disorder. Decreased volume of grey matter in the subgenual prefrontal cortex is found in unipolar and bipolar illnesses. Increased volume of amygdala is seen in bipolar illness.

questions.question_text: On MRI examination of the brain in depressive subjects, increased deep white matter hyperintensities are associated with:

options.text: Late-onset depression
Mild depression
Good treatment response
Psychomotor agitation
Personality disorder

correct_answer.text: Late-onset depression

correct_answers.text: Late-onset depression

questions.explanation: Increased deep white matter hyperintensities are also associated with vascular risk factors, severe depression, poor treatment response and psychomotor retardation.

questions.question_text: Neuropathological abnormalities observed in patients with mood disorders include which of the following?

options.text: Increased synaptic markers in the prefrontal cortex
Increased neuronal size in the prefrontal cortex
Increased neuronal density in the prefrontal cortex
Increased glial cell numbers in the cingulate cortex
None of the above

correct_answer.text: None of the above

correct_answers.text: None of the above

questions.explanation: All are decreased, not increased.

questions.question_text: In which of the following is there altered cerebral blood flow in patients with depression?

options.text: Prefrontal cortex
Anterior cingulate cortex
Thalamus
Caudate nucleus
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Altered blood flow and metabolism are observed in all the regions in a to d, as well as amygdala.

questions.question_text: Regarding lithium augmentation in depression, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: According to research evidence it is more effective than placebo
Most people respond with an amelioration of their depressive state within 24–48 hours after commencement of lithium
Unipolar depressed patients do not respond so well as bipolar patients
The dexamethasone suppression test is reliable in identifying patients likely to respond to lithium
It is effective only when lithium is combined with SSRIs

correct_answer.text: According to research evidence it is more effective than placebo

correct_answers.text: According to research evidence it is more effective than placebo

questions.explanation: Amelioration of the depressive state can occur within 24–48 hours after commencement of lithium but usually symptoms resolve over 2–3 weeks; unipolar patients respond as well as bipolar patients; there are no reliable clinical or biochemical predictors; the effect is not restricted to any particular class of antidepressants.

questions.question_text: There is no research evidence to support the claim that electro-convulsive therapy (ECT) is more effective than:

options.text: Simulated ECT in major depression
Tricyclic antidepressant treatment in major depression
MAOI antidepressant treatment in major depression
Antipsychotic treatment in depressive psychosis
Combined tricyclic antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment in depressive psychosis

correct_answer.text: Combined tricyclic antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment in depressive psychosis

correct_answers.text: Combined tricyclic antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment in depressive psychosis

questions.explanation: It has been observed that in depressive psychosis, combined tricyclic antidepressant and antipsychotic treatment may be as effective as ECT but there is no research evidence. There is research evidence for atod.

questions.question_text: Regarding longer-term treatment for mood disorders, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Continuing antidepressants for 6 months after remission decreases the relapse rate by 50%
Mood-incongruent psychotic features predict good response to lithium maintenance treatment
Use of lithium maintenance treatment in recurrent mood disorders reduces suicide rates
Carbamazepine is useful in prophylaxis of rapid cycling disorders
Lamotrigine is effective in prophylaxis of bipolar depression

correct_answer.text: Mood-incongruent psychotic features predict good response to lithium maintenance treatment

correct_answers.text: Mood-incongruent psychotic features predict good response to lithium maintenance treatment

questions.explanation: Mood-incongruent psychotic features predict poor response to lithium maintenance treatment.

questions.question_text: Common indications for treatment with SSRIs in depression include all of the following, except:

options.text: Significant history of heart disease
Concurrent treatment with anticholinergic drugs
Risk of overdose
Tendency to gain weight
Sedation desirable

correct_answer.text: Sedation desirable

correct_answers.text: Sedation desirable

questions.explanation: SSRIs are indicated for treatment of depression when sedation is undesirable.

questions.question_text: A 54-year-old woman is brought to the casualty department with acute onset of confusion and agitation. On examination she appears to be febrile, and has been sweating excessively. She is also found to have myoclonus and nystagmus. A careful history reveals that she has had chronic depression, hypertension and diabetes mellitus. She has been on insulin, phenelzine, atenolol and ramipril, and because of ongoing depressive symptoms clomipramine was added to her prescription recently. The most probable cause of her presentation is:

options.text: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Hypoglycaemia
Serotonin syndrome
Urinary tract infection
Wernicke's encephalopathy

correct_answer.text: Serotonin syndrome

correct_answers.text: Serotonin syndrome

questions.explanation: When serotoninergic drugs like clomipramine are combined with MAOIs like phenelzine, serotonin syndrome occurs, with the clinical features mentioned.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding velocardiofacial syndrome, except:

options.text: It is also known as DiGeorge syndrome
It is caused by deletion of one copy of chromosome 21
It is associated with cognitive impairment
70% of cases are associated with psychosis
It is a rare cause of schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: 70% of cases are associated with psychosis

correct_answers.text: 70% of cases are associated with psychosis

questions.explanation: 30% of cases are associated with schizophrenia-like or affective psychosis.

questions.question_text: Regarding antipsychotic treatments for schizophrenia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Drug treatment has more effect on positive symptoms than on negative symptoms
Antipsychotics given at the first sign of relapse are more effective than continuous prophylaxis
Depot medications are more effective in preventing relapse than oral medications
There is some research evidence favouring the use of atypical antipsychotics rather than typical ones in the prophylaxis of schizophrenia
The efficacy of clozapine is superior to that of other antipsychotics

correct_answer.text: Antipsychotics given at the first sign of relapse are more effective than continuous prophylaxis

correct_answers.text: Antipsychotics given at the first sign of relapse are more effective than continuous prophylaxis

questions.explanation: Continuous treatment is more effective than intermittent treatment.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding treatment with clozapine, except:

options.text: Clozapine has proven efficacy in treatment-resistant schizophrenia
Clozapine reduces mortality with suicide in schizophrenia
Clozapine may be useful in the first episode of schizophrenia in treatment-naive patients as clear superiority is proven in comparison with chlorpromazine
Antipsychotic polypharmacy may be justified in clozapine-resistant schizophrenia
In clozapine-resistant schizophrenia, augmentation with lamotrigine and valproate may be useful

correct_answer.text: Clozapine may be useful in the first episode of schizophrenia in treatment-naive patients as clear superiority is proven in comparison with chlorpromazine

correct_answers.text: Clozapine may be useful in the first episode of schizophrenia in treatment-naive patients as clear superiority is proven in comparison with chlorpromazine

questions.explanation: The superiority of clozapine in the first episode of schizophrenia in treatment-naive patients was not proven in a one-year trial.

questions.question_text: Regarding the management of acute episodes of schizophrenia, which of the following statements is not true?

options.text: Hospital admission is usually indicated in the first episode
A drug-free observation period may be helpful in the diagnosis
Antipsychotic medication should be initiated soon after diagnosis
In the acute phase, intramuscular medications are preferable to oral medications
Anticholinergic drugs should not be given routinely to prevent extrapyramidal symptoms

correct_answer.text: In the acute phase, intramuscular medications are preferable to oral medications

correct_answers.text: In the acute phase, intramuscular medications are preferable to oral medications

questions.explanation: Oral medications are always preferable, but intramuscular medications may be necessary to control disturbed behaviour in patients who are not compliant with oral treatment.

questions.question_text: Antipsychotic drugs are associated with all of the following, except:

options.text: Increased risk of cerebrovascular events
Insulin resistance
Dyslipidaemia
Osteoporosis
Shortened QTc interval

correct_answer.text: Shortened QTc interval

correct_answers.text: Shortened QTc interval

questions.explanation: Antipsychotic drugs cause a prolonged QTc interval. Osteoporosis can result from hyperprolactinaemia.

questions.question_text: Regarding the prognosis of schizophrenia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Early treatment is associated with better prognosis
Much of the deterioration in social functioning takes place later on in the illness, especially after 10 years
Good premorbid functioning is a risk factor for suicide
Patients with prolonged negative symptoms are less likely to attempt suicide
Clozapine treatment significantly reduces suicide risk in schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Much of the deterioration in social functioning takes place later on in the illness, especially after 10 years

correct_answers.text: Much of the deterioration in social functioning takes place later on in the illness, especially after 10 years

questions.explanation: Much of the deterioration in social functioning takes place in the first 2 years after diagnosis.

questions.question_text: Regarding the prognosis of schizophrenia, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Treatment response time increases with increasing number of relapses
According to an Epidemiologic Catchment Area (ECA) study in the USA, patients with schizophrenia have a four- to fivefold increased risk of substance abuse
In half of violent schizophrenic patients, the violent behaviour can be directly attributed to psychotic symptoms like delusions
Suicide risk is increased early in the course of the illness
The mortality rate in women with schizophrenia is twice that in men

correct_answer.text: The mortality rate in women with schizophrenia is twice that in men

correct_answers.text: The mortality rate in women with schizophrenia is twice that in men

questions.explanation: The mortality rate in men with schizophrenia is twice that in women.

questions.question_text: Regarding pathological jealousy, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Delusions of jealousy are more common in females with paranoid schizophrenia than in males with paranoid schizophrenia
Delusions of jealousy are more common in males with alcoholic psychosis than in females with alcoholic psychosis
The mainstay of treatment is antipsychotic drugs
If there is a risk of violence, the doctor should warn a partner (even if that means breaching confidentiality)
Patients usually respond very well to combined treatment with antipsychotics and cognitive behavioural therapy

correct_answer.text: Patients usually respond very well to combined treatment with antipsychotics and cognitive behavioural therapy

correct_answers.text: Patients usually respond very well to combined treatment with antipsychotics and cognitive behavioural therapy

questions.explanation: The general impression is that the prognosis is poor and only marginal benefits are reported with treatment.

questions.question_text: Regarding head injury, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: The duration of post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) is a good indicator of the severity of a closed head injury
PTA of less than 1 week indicates a better chance of returning to work
Retrograde amnesia is a better predictor of outcome than PTA
Deposition of beta amyloid may explain the link between head injury and Alzheimer's disease
Apolipoprotein E4 genotype may increase the risk of death after head injury

correct_answer.text: Retrograde amnesia is a better predictor of outcome than PTA

correct_answers.text: Retrograde amnesia is a better predictor of outcome than PTA

questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia has less predictive value.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding postconcussion syndrome are true, except:

options.text: It is associated with anxiety and depression
It is accompanied by headache and difficulties in concentration
It occurs only after severe head injury
It can be of psychological origin
It mostly resolves without treatment

correct_answer.text: It occurs only after severe head injury

correct_answers.text: It occurs only after severe head injury

questions.explanation: Postconcussion syndrome often occurs after mild head injury.

questions.question_text: Regarding Gilles de la Tourette syndrome, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Multiple tics begin before the age of 16
30% of people with the syndrome have coprolalia
Obsessive compulsive symptoms are seen
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder occurs frequently
Antipsychotics are contraindicated

correct_answer.text: Antipsychotics are contraindicated

correct_answers.text: Antipsychotics are contraindicated

questions.explanation: Haloperidol and risperidone are an effective treatment; echolalia and echopraxia occur in 10–40%.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding multiple sclerosis, except:

options.text: Psychological symptoms appear in two-thirds of patients
Psychological symptoms are usually the presenting features
It is associated with increased risk of suicide
Rapidly progressive dementia may occur
Cognitive impairment correlates with the degree of callosal atrophy

correct_answer.text: Psychological symptoms are usually the presenting features

correct_answers.text: Psychological symptoms are usually the presenting features

questions.explanation: Psychological symptoms are rarely the presenting features.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding anorexia nervosa?

options.text: Amenorrhoea precedes weight loss in 50% of patients
Lack of sexual interest is usual
High levels of T3 and T4 with low levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) are a usual biochemical finding
Decreased growth hormone concentration occurs
25% of patients eventually develop schizophrenia

correct_answer.text: Lack of sexual interest is usual

correct_answers.text: Lack of sexual interest is usual

questions.explanation: Amenorrhoea precedes weight loss in 20% of patients; low levels of T3 and low normal T4 with normal TSH is a usual biochemical finding; raised growth hormone concentration is seen. Anorexia does not evolve into schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Regarding the prognosis of anorexia nervosa, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: It is associated with a sixfold increase in mortality
The usual causes of death include suicide
20% of patients recover fully
20% of patients remain severely ill
Onset at a younger age is a bad prognostic indicator

correct_answer.text: Onset at a younger age is a bad prognostic indicator

correct_answers.text: Onset at a younger age is a bad prognostic indicator

questions.explanation: Onset at a younger age is associated with better prognosis.

questions.question_text: All of the following are abnormalities found in anorexia nervosa, except:

options.text: Low concentrations of luteinizing hormone
Increased plasma cortisol
Dexamethasone non-suppression
Hypercholesterolaemia
Hyperkalaemia

correct_answer.text: Hyperkalaemia

correct_answers.text: Hyperkalaemia

questions.explanation: Hypokalaemia occurs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding restoration of weight in anorexia nervosa?

options.text: It is usually done as an outpatient
The aim is to increase body weight by 0.5 kg a week
It requires an extra 500–1000 calories per day
The usual target weight is between a healthy weight and a weight the patient thinks is ideal
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Inpatient admission is indicated where there are life-threatening physical complications, severe depression and increased suicidal risk.

questions.question_text: Regarding the management of bulimia nervosa, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: The most effective treatment is a special form of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT)
30–50% of patients improve with therapy
SSRIs do not appear to be beneficial as treatment
A treatment combination of CBT and antidepressants does not have any advantage over treatment with CBT alone
Interpersonal psychotherapy may be as effective as CBT, but takes longer to be effective

correct_answer.text: SSRIs do not appear to be beneficial as treatment

correct_answers.text: SSRIs do not appear to be beneficial as treatment

questions.explanation: SSRIs decrease the frequency of binge eating and purging and help in improving the mood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Kleine–Levin syndrome?

options.text: It consists of episodes of sleep lasting for days or weeks with long periods of normality in between
Increased appetite occurs
Hypothalamic dysfunction is suggested in the aetiology
Lithium may be useful in the treatment
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: An autonomic basis is proposed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding sleepwalking disorder?

options.text: It is more common in children between 5 and 12 years of age
It may be familial
It occurs in approximately 15% of children
It rarely lasts as much as an hour
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: An episode of sleepwalking disorder usually lasts for only a few seconds or minutes, and rarely lasts up to an hour.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding suicide are correct, except:

options.text: 30–50% of people who commit suicide are diagnosed with personality disorder
10% of people with mood disorder die by suicide
There are higher rates in male doctors than female doctors
In most countries, the highest rate is reported in the population above 75 years old
Rates among adolescents have increased recently

correct_answer.text: 10% of people with mood disorder die by suicide

correct_answers.text: 10% of people with mood disorder die by suicide

questions.explanation: 6% of people with mood disorder die by suicide.

questions.question_text: Regarding psychiatric aspects of pregnancy, all of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Psychiatric disorder is more common in the second trimester than in the first and third
Women with chronic psychological problems may improve during pregnancy
Eating disorders are not precipitated by pregnancy
Pseudocyesis is more common in younger women
In Couvade syndrome, the man complains of morning sickness

correct_answer.text: Psychiatric disorder is more common in the second trimester than in the first and third

correct_answers.text: Psychiatric disorder is more common in the second trimester than in the first and third

questions.explanation: Psychiatric disorder is more common in the first and third trimester than in the second trimester.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding premenstrual syndrome?

options.text: It may present with a craving for food
There is decreased prevalence in those around 30 years of age
Lack of oestrogen and excess progesterone have been postulated as an aetiological mechanism
There is a low response rate to placebo
Bromocriptine is the only effective treatment

correct_answer.text: It may present with a craving for food

correct_answers.text: It may present with a craving for food

questions.explanation: There is increased prevalence in those around 30 years of age; lack of progesterone and excess oestrogen have been postulated as an aetiological mechanism; there is a high response rate to placebo; bromocriptine is used in treatment, but no drugs have been proven to be effective.

questions.question_text: All of the following are associated with premenstrual syndrome, except:

options.text: EEG changes
Alteration in response to dichotic auditory stimuli
Alterations in skin conductance
Type A behaviour
High CNS beta endorphin levels

correct_answer.text: High CNS beta endorphin levels

correct_answers.text: High CNS beta endorphin levels

questions.explanation: Low CNS beta endorphin levels are associated with premenstrual syndrome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is useful in treating premenstrual syndrome?

options.text: SSRIs
Oral contraceptive pill
Vitamin B6
Diuretics
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Bromocriptine and benzodiazepines are also used.

questions.question_text: All of the following are features of cyclic psychosis, except:

options.text: Psychotic symptoms appearing suddenly before menstruation
Tonic–clonic fits
Transitory EEG abnormalities
Psychomotor retardation
Amnesia

correct_answer.text: Tonic–clonic fits

correct_answers.text: Tonic–clonic fits

questions.explanation: EEG abnormalities not amounting to epilepsy can occur.

questions.question_text: The recommended treatment for cyclic psychosis includes:

options.text: Bromocriptine
Progesterone
Clomiphene citrate
Acetazolamide
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Bromocriptine reduces prolactin and progesterone inhibits ovulation; psychotropic drugs are also used.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is associated with miscarriage?

options.text: Severe life events in the 3 months before miscarriage
Childhood maternal separation
Poor relationship with partners
Few social contacts
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Major social difficulty and severe short-term life event in the first 2 weeks immediately prior miscarriage are associated with miscarriage.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding postnatal blues, except:

options.text: Peak incidence occurs between 3 and 5 days in the postpartum period
They are associated with a history of premenstrual tension
Serum calcium may play a role in their occurrence
They are associated with a history of poor marital relationship
They occur in about 80% of mothers

correct_answer.text: They occur in about 80% of mothers

correct_answers.text: They occur in about 80% of mothers

questions.explanation: Postnatal blues occur in half of mothers.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding postpartum depression, except:

options.text: It occurs in 10–15% of mothers
It usually occurs in the first 3 months postpartum
There is an increased incidence in multiparous women
Past psychiatric history is a risk factor
The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale is useful in identifying cases

correct_answer.text: There is an increased incidence in multiparous women

correct_answers.text: There is an increased incidence in multiparous women

questions.explanation: It was not observed to be associated with parity.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding the management of postnatal depression, except:

options.text: Counselling by health visitors is effective
Self-help groups are useful
Antidepressants may be required
ECT is recommended in severe cases
Lithium is routinely given, as it has been proven effective

correct_answer.text: Lithium is routinely given, as it has been proven effective

correct_answers.text: Lithium is routinely given, as it has been proven effective

questions.explanation: Lithium is not usually given, as it is secreted in the breast milk and is toxic to the child.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding postnatal depression?

options.text: It may last for a few years
It can cause cognitive abnormalities in children of affected mothers
There is a raised risk for further episodes of postnatal depression
It is associated with an increased rate of thyroid dysfunction in the postpartum year
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Postpartum thyroid dysfunction peaks at 4–5 months.

questions.question_text: All of the following are features of puerperal psychosis, except:

options.text: Onset is gradual, in the first few months after childbirth
It is not associated with cognitive impairment
The majority of cases are affective psychosis
It is more common in primipara
There is an increased occurrence in higher social classes

correct_answer.text: Onset is gradual, in the first few months after childbirth

correct_answers.text: Onset is gradual, in the first few months after childbirth

questions.explanation: Onset is abrupt, in the first few weeks.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true regarding puerperal psychosis, except:

options.text: There is a higher risk in women with schizophrenia than in women with bipolar illness
Most patients recover fully
Most sufferers are capable of looking after their baby with support
Joint admission with the baby may reduce the duration of illness and relapse rate
ECT is often the best treatment in severe cases

correct_answer.text: There is a higher risk in women with schizophrenia than in women with bipolar illness

correct_answers.text: There is a higher risk in women with schizophrenia than in women with bipolar illness

questions.explanation: Risk is higher in bipolar illness than in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: In the assessment of sexual dysfunction, each partner should be asked:

options.text: Whether the problem has occurred with more than one partner
About masturbation
About frequency of intercourse
The sexual techniques of the other partner
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: Each partner should also be asked about sexual thoughts, feelings, social relationships, etc.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding sex therapy?

options.text: It involves education about the anatomy and physiology of intercourse
It is not helpful in the majority of patients
Better results are obtained if couples are treated separately
A spectator role is encouraged in graded tasks
If successful, the improvement is usually sustained for years

correct_answer.text: It involves education about the anatomy and physiology of intercourse

correct_answers.text: It involves education about the anatomy and physiology of intercourse

questions.explanation: Sex therapy is successful in 30% of cases and there is some improvement in a further 30%; better results are obtained if a couple are treated together; the 'spectator role' is checking their own arousal, which has an inhibitory effect and should be discouraged; improvement is usually maintained for months and seldom for more than 3 years.

questions.question_text: In a psychotherapeutic intervention, a patient tells you about her experience of her boss shouting at her because she arrived late at the office on one occasion. You say, 'It must have been really difficult for you. I can understand why you feel anxious about that.' This is an example of:

options.text: Interpretation
Affirmation
Clarification
Advice and praise
Empathic validation

correct_answer.text: Empathic validation

correct_answers.text: Empathic validation

questions.explanation: Empathic validation helps patients to feel that the therapist understands their inner feelings and they are more likely to accept interpretations.

questions.question_text: A depressed 44-year-old woman who has come for her first session of psychotherapy gets worked up because her husband is late in coming to the hospital to pick her up. She becomes tearful and tells the receptionist that she is worried that he has been involved in an accident. This is an example of:

options.text: Interpretation
Exaggeration
Catastrophizing
Overgeneralizing
Ignoring the positive

correct_answer.text: Catastrophizing

correct_answers.text: Catastrophizing

questions.explanation: It is one of the logical errors occurring in depressive disorders.

questions.question_text: All of the following are therapeutic factors in group therapy, except:

options.text: Shared experience
Formation of subgroups
Group cohesion
Interpersonal learning
Recapitulation of the family group

correct_answer.text: Formation of subgroups

correct_answers.text: Formation of subgroups

questions.explanation: Formation of subgroups disrupts the therapeutic process.

questions.question_text: The underlying principles of therapeutic community include:

options.text: Democracy
Reality confrontation
Permissiveness
Community
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

correct_answers.text: All of the above

questions.explanation: These principles can lead to features like shared decisions and shared activities.

questions.question_text: Bloch and Harari's framework for assessment of family function includes all of the following, except:

options.text: Family structure recorded in the genogram
Changes and events, including financial problems
Relationships (including conflicts)
Patterns of interaction involving two or more people in the family
Role of transference in shaping the interactions between family members

correct_answer.text: Role of transference in shaping the interactions between family members

correct_answers.text: Role of transference in shaping the interactions between family members

questions.explanation: The important questions addressed in the framework are (1) 'How does the family function?' (choices a to d are included in this); and (2) 'Are family factors involved in the patient's problems?' (this is assessed by questions dealing with how the family is reacting, supporting the patient and contributing to the problem).

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about Hypericum perforatum, except:

options.text: It is more effective than placebo in moderate depression
The most common side-effects include gastrointestinal disturbances
It may induce mania
It is a hepatic enzyme inducer
It is safe to use with SSRIs

correct_answer.text: It is safe to use with SSRIs

correct_answers.text: It is safe to use with SSRIs

questions.explanation: Hypericum perforatum is commonly known as St John's wort; it may cause serotonin toxicity when combined with SSRIs.

questions.question_text: The risk of Ebstein's anomaly associated with first-trimester use of lithium is:

options.text: 1/200 births
1/2000 births
1/20 000 births
1/200 000 births
1/100 000 births

correct_answer.text: 1/2000 births

correct_answers.text: 1/2000 births

questions.explanation: Risk in the general population is 1/20 000 and there is a 10-fold increase with lithium use.

questions.question_text: The neural-tube defects in offspring associated with valproate use in the first trimester of pregnancy could be as high as:
questions.explanation: Spina bifida occurs and it is suggested that supplemental folate may reduce the risk.

questions.question_text: Use of which of the following in pregnancy is associated with the highest risk of congenital malformation in children?

options.text: Lithium
Carbamazepine
Valproate
Lamotrigine
e.b,c and d carry equal risk

correct_answer.text: Valproate

correct_answers.text: Valproate

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine has a 2.3% risk, lamotrigine 3%, and valproate 7.2%.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding atomoxetine are true, except:

options.text: It is a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor
It is licensed for treatment of ADHD
Sleep disturbance is a common side-effect
Hepatic damage is a rare side-effect
It is safe in angle-closure glaucoma

correct_answer.text: It is safe in angle-closure glaucoma

correct_answers.text: It is safe in angle-closure glaucoma

questions.explanation: Atomoxetine can worsen as well as potentially cause angle-closure glaucoma in susceptible individuals.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements regarding Huntington's disease are true, except:

options.text: Initial insight may result in depression
Schizophrenia-like psychosis occurs
Serpentine tongue is a typical feature
There is an increased concentration of GABA in the caudate nucleus
Gaze apraxia is found

correct_answer.text: There is an increased concentration of GABA in the caudate nucleus

correct_answers.text: There is an increased concentration of GABA in the caudate nucleus

questions.explanation: There is a decreased concentration of GABA in the caudate nucleus.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding Huntington's disease?

options.text: The gene is located on chromosome 16
The average time to death after diagnosis is 5 years
It is associated with increased risk of suicide
An increased volume of caudate is observed
It causes rapidly progressing dementia

correct_answer.text: It is associated with increased risk of suicide

correct_answers.text: It is associated with increased risk of suicide

questions.explanation: The average time to death after diagnosis is 12–16 years; decreased volume of caudate is observed; it causes slowly progressing dementia.

questions.question_text: HIV dementia is associated with which of the following?

options.text: Reduced libido early on
Incontinence
Ataxia
Hyperreflexia
All of the above

correct_answer.text: All of the above

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding HIV infection?

options.text: Associated dementia occurs in 50% of HIV-infected patients
The most common infection is cytomegalovirus infection of the central nervous system
Dementia is slowly progressing
A progression from mild neurocognitive disorder to dementia cannot be prevented by antiviral treatment
Depression is more common in men than in women

correct_answer.text: Associated dementia occurs in 50% of HIV-infected patients

correct_answers.text: Associated dementia occurs in 50% of HIV-infected patients

questions.explanation: The most common infection is Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia; dementia is rapidly progressing, with death occurring in 50–75% of cases within 6 months; progression from mild neurocognitive disorder can be prevented by treatment; depression is more common in women than in men.

questions.question_text: Protease inhibitors increase the concentration of all the following, except:

options.text: SSRIs
Aripiprazole
Valproate
Zolpidem
Bupropion

correct_answer.text: Valproate

correct_answers.text: Valproate

questions.explanation: Protease inhibitors induce the metabolism of valproate and alprazolam, and reduce their concentration.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a protease inhibitor?

options.text: Zidovudine
Zalcitabine
Nevirapine
Delavirdine
Ritonavir

correct_answer.text: Ritonavir

correct_answers.text: Ritonavir

questions.explanation: Zidovudine and zalcitabine are nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors. Nevirapine and delavirdine are non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors. Triple therapy is a combination of two reverse transcriptase inhibitors and a protease inhibitor.
